screening_decisions.reason: Retrospective observational study comparing appropriate vs inappropriate initial therapy, not an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy.
Open non-comparative study focusing on staphylococcal osteoarticular infections, not an RCT and wrong population/intervention.
RCT comparing gentamicin dosing regimens for acute pyelonephritis, wrong population (not sepsis/septic shock) and wrong intervention.
Observational study analyzing hospital charges and length of stay associated with antimicrobial regimen changes, not an RCT.
Clinical practice guidelines developed via Delphi method, not an RCT.
Cross-sectional observational study of antibiotic prescription patterns in ICUs, not an RCT.
Population-based descriptive study on epidemiology and costs of severe sepsis, not an RCT.
Editorial/review article discussing a treatment paradigm, not an RCT.
Retrospective review assessing de-escalation rates in severe nosocomial sepsis, not an RCT.
Observational study of antimicrobial use in a Danish ICU, not an RCT.
Review article on sepsis management and antibiotic therapy, not an RCT.
RCT evaluating procalcitonin-guided antibiotic duration vs standard guidelines, intervention does not match de-escalation based on culture results.
Observational substudy analyzing the impact of adequate vs inadequate empiric therapy on survival, not an RCT comparing de-escalation strategies.
Prospective observational study on compliance with antimicrobial guidelines, not an RCT.
Review article on optimizing antimicrobial therapy in sepsis, not an RCT.
Review article on antibiotic use in surgical infections, not an RCT.
Observational cohort study comparing PCT and CRP levels in sepsis/MODS, not an RCT.
Methodological paper on quantifying heterogeneity in meta-analyses, completely irrelevant to the clinical question.
Review article on therapeutic challenges in gram-negative sepsis, not an RCT.
Prospective observational study evaluating biomarkers for predicting infected necrosis in acute pancreatitis, wrong population and not an RCT.
This is a review article discussing imipenem as an agent for de-escalation therapy, not a randomized controlled trial. It does not compare de-escalation versus standard therapy in a trial design.
This is a review article about antimicrobial streamlining for lower respiratory tract infections, not an RCT. The population is LRTI patients, not specifically sepsis/septic shock.
This is a review article summarizing pharmacokinetic studies and dosing recommendations, not an RCT comparing de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is an RCT but in preterm infants (not adults). The intervention compares dosing frequency, not de-escalation based on culture results versus standard therapy.
This is a review article about carbapenem patents and antibacterial effects, not an RCT.
This is a review article providing principles for antimicrobial dosing, not an RCT comparing de-escalation versus standard therapy.

This is an RCT in ICU patients, but the intervention is procalcitonin-guided diagnostics and treatment, not de-escalation based on culture results. The comparison is PCT-guided vs standard care, not de-escalation vs standard therapy.
This is a retrospective cohort study, not an RCT. It examines the association between delays in antimicrobial therapy and AKI outcomes, not de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is a descriptive article about the implementation of the Surviving Sepsis Campaign in Brazil, not an RCT.
This is a laboratory/microbiology study characterizing a beta-lactamase gene, not an RCT.
This is an observational study with a pharmacist-based intervention, not an RCT. It focuses on redundant antibiotic combinations, not de-escalation based on culture results.

This is an RCT in surgical ICU patients, but the intervention is PCT-guided duration of antibiotic therapy, not de-escalation based on culture results. The population is not specifically sepsis/septic shock patients.
This is a review article about UTIs, not an RCT. The condition is UTI, not sepsis/septic shock.
This is a retrospective cohort study, not an RCT. It examines the association between initial antimicrobial treatment appropriateness and mortality, not de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is a methodological paper about reporting standards for RCTs, not an RCT itself.
This is a retrospective case record study about bacterial meningitis, not an RCT. The condition is meningitis, not sepsis/septic shock.
This is a review article about empiric antibiotic selection, not an RCT. It actually states that de-escalation is not necessary if initial monotherapy was wisely selected.
This is a letter/commentary about a meta-analysis, not an RCT.
This is a methodological paper about a severity scoring system, not an RCT.
This is a guidelines/SOP document for antibiotic administration in injured patients, not an RCT. The population is severely injured patients, not specifically sepsis/septic shock.

This is an RCT but does not meet selection criteria. The population is ICU patients with pulmonary infiltrates, not specifically sepsis/severe sepsis/septic shock. The intervention uses CPIS score (clinical pulmonary infection score) for decision-making, not culture results for de-escalation. The study compares short-course ciprofloxacin monotherapy vs standard therapy, not de-escalation based on culture results.

This is explicitly a retrospective study, not an RCT. The abstract states 'retrospective monocentric study' and 'we compared the characteristics and outcome of patients who have experienced de-escalation therapy with those who have not.' This is an observational comparison, not a randomized trial.

This is a review/guideline article, not an RCT. The abstract discusses guidelines and recommendations for antibiotic therapy in critically ill patients. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.

This is a review/guideline article, not an RCT. The abstract discusses management principles and recommendations for antibiotic therapy in septic shock patients. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.

This is a before-after study of a restrictive antibiotic policy, not an RCT. The population is elderly care unit patients, not specifically sepsis/severe sepsis/septic shock. The intervention is a policy change, not de-escalation based on culture results.

This is a retrospective review of microbiologic culture results, not an RCT. The study reviews 5-year culture data from hemodialysis patients with catheter-related bacteremia. No intervention or randomized trial methodology is described.

This is a review article (PURPOSE OF REVIEW stated), not an RCT. The abstract reviews recent data on Pseudomonas aeruginosa infections in critically ill patients. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.

This is a retrospective review, not an RCT. The abstract states 'A retrospective review of our rapid response system database was performed.' The study compares adequacy of empiric therapy before and after algorithm implementation, not de-escalation vs standard therapy.
This is a review/guideline article, not an RCT. The abstract discusses principles of antibiotic therapy for bacterial endocarditis. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.
This is a review article, not an RCT. The abstract discusses management principles for severe skin and soft tissue infections. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.
This is a review article, not an RCT. The abstract discusses sepsis treatment principles and recommendations. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.

This is a commentary/letter, not an RCT. The abstract discusses procalcitonin levels in liver transplant patients and references another study. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.

This is a secondary analysis of a clinical trial, not an RCT comparing de-escalation vs standard therapy. The study examines the effect of inappropriate initial antimicrobial therapy on prognosis. Importantly, the selection criteria explicitly exclude 'Studies including patients initially treated with an empirical but not adequate antimicrobial therapy' - this study specifically includes and analyzes patients with inappropriate (inadequate) initial therapy.
This is a review article, not an RCT. Additionally, the population is neonates, not adults as required by the selection criteria. The abstract discusses antibiotic use in neonatal sepsis.

This is a prospective observational cohort study, not an RCT. The abstract states 'DESIGN Prospective observational cohort study.' The study investigates procalcitonin as a predictor of mortality, not de-escalation vs standard therapy.

This is an RCT but does not meet selection criteria. The study compares bolus dosing vs continuous infusion of piperacillin-tazobactam, not de-escalation based on culture results vs standard therapy. The intervention is about dosing strategy, not de-escalation.

This is a review article (PURPOSE OF REVIEW stated), not an RCT. The abstract reviews approaches to reduce antibiotic resistance in ICU patients. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.

This is a prospective observational study, not an RCT. The abstract states 'DESIGN AND SETTING Prospective, observational study' and 'INTERVENTIONS None.' The study describes epidemiology of severe sepsis, not de-escalation vs standard therapy.
This is a review article, not an RCT. The abstract summarizes properties of systemic antibiotics recently marketed and in development. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.

This appears to be the Cochrane review protocol/abstract itself (title matches the review title exactly, and 'cochranelibrary.com' is in the abstract). This is not a primary RCT but rather the systematic review protocol. No primary data or randomized trial methodology is described.
This is a review/opinion article discussing carbapenem use in ICU infections. It is not an RCT and does not compare de-escalation versus standard therapy.

This is an observational description of an antimicrobial stewardship program using PCT to discontinue antibiotics. It is not an RCT, and the intervention is discontinuation rather than de-escalation based on culture results.
This is a retrospective cohort study examining timing of antimicrobial therapy initiation. It is not an RCT and does not address de-escalation.
This is a retrospective study in neonatal patients (extremely low birth weight infants), not adults. It is not an RCT and does not address de-escalation.
This is a review article discussing antifungal strategies. It is not an RCT and focuses on fungal infections rather than bacterial sepsis de-escalation.
This is an observational study on community-acquired pneumonia, not sepsis. It is not an RCT and does not address de-escalation.
This is a large observational cohort study describing sepsis incidence and characteristics. It is not an RCT and does not compare interventions.
This is an observational study evaluating the impact of an infectious disease service. It is not an RCT and does not compare de-escalation versus standard therapy.
This is a point-prevalence study describing ICU-acquired infections. It is not an RCT and does not compare interventions.

This appears to be a very brief communication or opinion piece about de-escalation in ventilator-associated pneumonia. There is no indication it is an RCT, and it focuses on VAP rather than general sepsis.
This is a review article on UTI diagnosis and management. It is not an RCT and does not address sepsis de-escalation.
This is a consensus conference report defining sepsis terminology. It is not an RCT and does not compare interventions.

This is a prospective observational study on de-escalation in ventilator-associated pneumonia. While it addresses de-escalation, it is not an RCT and focuses on VAP rather than general sepsis/septic shock.
This is a review article summarizing evidence for sepsis management recommendations. It is not an RCT.
This is a methodological paper on clinical measurements in cardiology. It is completely unrelated to sepsis or antimicrobial therapy.
This is a prospective cohort study in neonatal patients, not adults. It is not an RCT and actually focuses on inadequate empiric therapy (which would be excluded per criteria).

This is an RCT in adults with severe sepsis, but the intervention is PCT-guided discontinuation of antibiotics, not de-escalation based on culture results. The intervention differs from the review question which specifies de-escalation (narrowing spectrum) based on culture results.

This is an RCT in adult ICU patients, but the intervention is selective decontamination of the digestive tract (prophylactic antibiotics), not de-escalation of systemic antimicrobial therapy based on culture results.
This is an observational cross-sectional study on sepsis prevalence. It is not an RCT and does not compare interventions.
This is a review article on antibiotic dosing in CRRT patients. It is not an RCT and does not address de-escalation.
